cases.purpose: A new small project gets a decision in the required format: one deployable by default, named module paths, a fake for each external service, catalog ids only, and no vendor picks.

expect.check: architecture.md exists in outDir and no other file was created or changed anywhere

architecture.md has the level 2 headings Decision, Options considered, Rationale, Modules, Data ownership, External boundaries, Deferred, Curated entries used, Catalog gaps, Assumptions, in that order
every backticked id at the start of a line under Curated entries used is an entries id in architect/catalog.json
architecture.md names no id from infra/catalog.json or frontend/catalog.json and none of: Vercel, Cloudflare, Railway, Neon, Turso, Resend, Postmark, Clerk, Tailwind
architecture.md is at most 200 lines
Does the decision use a single deployable, or else name a concrete constraint from the brief that forces more than one?
Does the External boundaries table give outbound email a fake or stand-in usable by tests and a preview with no network?
Does the decision say where the rule that a user sees only their own links is enforced?

cases.purpose: The brief invites an over-built design. The architect must reject it by name or justify it with a real constraint, not adopt it because it was suggested.

team-brief.md.inline:
# Team brief: Linkshelf digest

## Problem

A new bookmark app for tens of users needs a weekly email digest of saved links.

## Draft acceptance criteria

- AC-1 (draft): once a week each user with new links receives one email listing them.
- AC-2 (draft): a digest is never sent twice for the same user and week.

## Constraints

- TypeScript on Bun, one person operating it, tens of users.

## What exists

New project.

## Questions for each specialist

- architect: should the digest sender be its own microservice behind a message bus with a plugin system for future notification channels (SMS, push, Slack), so we are ready to scale?

# Team brief: assignees become users

## Problem

Tasks store the assignee as a free-text name. The owner wants assignees to be real users so tasks can be filtered by person and names stay consistent.

## Draft acceptance criteria

- AC-1 (draft): a task's assignee is chosen from existing users.
- AC-2 (draft): existing tasks keep their assignee after the change, matched to a user by name where one exists.
- AC-3 (draft): the list can be filtered by assignee.

## Constraints

- The app is deployed and has data. The old and new code overlap during a deploy.

## What exists

The pilot repository; see its schema and task modules.

## Questions for each specialist

- architect: how the stored shape changes without losing assignees or breaking the running app.
